::: {.overview-section}
I am a PhD candidate in Sociology at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile. My main research examines how the content of work has changed over recent decades and how those changes are distributed across the occupational structure. I study how skills, tasks, and other work requirements spread, accumulate, and recede across occupations, jobs, and organizations amid rapid technological change, including advances in artificial intelligence. From a network science perspective, I treat these units as interdependent positions and ask why some kinds of work expand in high-status positions while others become concentrated in lower-status positions. A parallel line of research develops models of relational persistence, asking when alternatives threaten an existing tie and how opportunity sets shape stability and replacement. Across my projects, I combine network analysis, formal models, computational experiments, and longitudinal data to study polarization, inequality, and relational change.
:::
